routes.label: Compare the two specified hand positions

question: It is now between \(10{:}00\) and \(11{:}00\) o’clock, and six minutes from now, the minute hand of a watch will be exactly opposite the place where the hour hand was three minutes ago. What is the exact time now?
solution:
The two positions occur at different times, so express each using the present time. Let \(t\) be the number of minutes after \(10{:}00\) now, with \(0<t<60\). Measure angles clockwise from \(12\).

The minute hand travels \(360/60=6\) degrees per minute. The hour hand travels \(30/60=\frac12\) degree per minute. Thus the hour hand's angle three minutes ago was
\[
H=300+\frac{t-3}{2},
\]
and the minute hand's angle six minutes from now, retaining any completed turn, is
\[
M=6(t+6).
\]
Their difference is
\[
M-H=\frac{11t-525}{2}.
\]
For \(0<t<60\), this lies strictly between \(-262.5^\circ\) and \(67.5^\circ\). Opposite positions have angle differences \(180^\circ\) plus an integer number of full turns. The only such difference in this range is \(-180^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\frac{11t-525}{2}=-180,
\qquad 11t=165,
\qquad t=15.
\]
As a check, at \(10{:}12\) the hour hand is at \(306^\circ\), while at \(10{:}21\) the minute hand is at \(126^\circ\), exactly opposite. The time now is \(\boxed{10{:}15}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
